author: DaveyD347
description: Detects creation of a minidump file whose name references LSASS. This is the artifact left by Task Manager's "Create dump file", ProcDump, comsvcs MiniDump, and most credential-dumping scripts, so it catches the outcome even when the dumping method is new.
false_positives: Support engineers collecting LSASS dumps for Microsoft troubleshooting; these should be ticketed and rare.
name: LSASS Dump File Written to Disk
query: (file.path:*\\lsass* AND (file.path:(*.dmp OR *.dump OR *.mdmp))) AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:*\\WerFault.exe AND file.path:*\\CrashDumps\\*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Every legitimate handle request reaches the kernel through ntdll.dll, so the first frame of a Sysmon CallTrace is an ntdll (or win32u) address. Tools such as Dumpert, NanoDump and SysWhispers-based loaders issue the syscall instruction from their own code to step around user-mode EDR hooks; Sysmon then records the tool's own module as the first frame. That evasion is itself the detection.
false_positives: Security products that deliberately use direct syscalls; identify them during baselining and exclude by SourceImage.
name: LSASS Opened via Direct System Call
query: (winlog.event_data.TargetImage:*\\lsass.exe AND winlog.event_data.CallTrace:*\|*) AND (NOT (winlog.event_data.CallTrace:(C\:\\Windows\\System32\\ntdll.dll\+* OR C\:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\ntdll.dll\+* OR C\:\\Windows\\System32\\win32u.dll\+*)))

author: DaveyD347
description: Sysmon records the call stack of every LSASS handle request. A frame marked UNKNOWN means the request came from memory that is not backed by a file on disk: shellcode, a reflectively loaded DLL, or an in-memory PowerShell assembly such as Invoke-Mimikatz. Legitimate software opens LSASS from code that lives in a signed module, so an unbacked frame is a strong signal regardless of which tool is used. Only the *direct* caller matters: the frame right after ntdll and KERNELBASE. .NET applications (Azure guest agent, PowerShell remoting hosts) also show UNKNOWN frames, but deeper in the stack, where JIT-compiled managed code calls framework methods that open the handle. Replay against the OTRF datasets surfaced exactly that noise from a naive "contains UNKNOWN". The regex avoids ^, $, \s, \d and lookarounds and is wrapped in .* so it behaves the same in PCRE (Splunk), RE2 (KQL) and Lucene's anchored regex dialect (Elastic).
false_positives: Some EDR and anti-cheat products open LSASS from unpacked code; baseline and exclude by SourceImage hash.
name: LSASS Accessed From Unbacked (Injected) Memory
query: winlog.event_data.TargetImage:*\\lsass.exe AND winlog.event_data.CallTrace:/.*ntdll\.dll\+[0-9a-fA-F]+\|[^|]*KERNELBASE\.dll\+[0-9a-fA-F]+\|UNKNOWN.*/

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects bitsadmin creating a transfer job that pulls a file over HTTP(S). BITS jobs survive reboots, run inside svchost and are often missed by proxy logging tuned for browsers, which makes them a convenient ingress channel.
false_positives: Legacy software updaters; modern Windows components use the BITS API, not the bitsadmin binary.
name: File Download via bitsadmin
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\bitsadmin.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:bitsadmin.exe) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-transfer\ * OR *\ \/transfer\ * OR *\ –transfer\ * OR *\ —transfer\ * OR *\ ―transfer\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-create\ * OR *\ \/create\ * OR *\ –create\ * OR *\ —create\ * OR *\ ―create\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-addfile\ * OR *\ \/addfile\ * OR *\ –addfile\ * OR *\ —addfile\ * OR *\ ―addfile\ *)) AND (process.command_line:(*http\:\/\/* OR *https\:\/\/*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects cmstp.exe silently installing a Connection Manager INF file. Malicious INFs use RunPreSetupCommands to execute arbitrary commands, and the /au variant auto-elevates through a COM interface to bypass UAC.
false_positives: VPN clients deployed with Connection Manager profiles; exclude their known INF paths.
name: CMSTP Silent INF Profile Install
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\cmstp.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:CMSTP.EXE) AND process.command_line:(*\ \-s\ * OR *\ \/s\ * OR *\ –s\ * OR *\ —s\ * OR *\ ―s\ *) AND process.command_line:*.inf*

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects esentutl copying SAM, SYSTEM, SECURITY or ntds.dit. With /vss, esentutl reads the file through a shadow copy, bypassing the lock the OS holds on these databases.
false_positives: None expected.
name: Locked Credential Store Copied via esentutl
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\esentutl.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:esentutl.exe) AND process.command_line:(*\ \-y\ * OR *\ \/y\ * OR *\ –y\ * OR *\ —y\ * OR *\ ―y\ *) AND (process.command_line:(*\/config\/sam* OR *\\config\\sam* OR *\/config\/system* OR *\\config\\system* OR *\/config\/security* OR *\\config\\security* OR *ntds.dit*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects rundll32 loading comsvcs.dll and calling its MiniDump export, a living-off-the-land way to write a full memory dump of a process (almost always LSASS) without dropping a dumping tool. The export can be referenced by name or by ordinal (#24), so both forms are covered.
false_positives: None known; comsvcs MiniDump has no legitimate administrative use on endpoints.
name: LSASS Memory Dump via comsvcs.dll MiniDump
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\rundll32.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:RUNDLL32.EXE) AND process.command_line:*comsvcs* AND (process.command_line:(*MiniDump* OR *#24* OR *#\+24* OR *#\-4294967272*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects mshta.exe given a vbscript: or javascript: protocol handler on the command line. This runs script directly from the command line, with no .hta file on disk, and is a common way to proxy a PowerShell or COM scriptlet payload through a signed Microsoft binary.
false_positives: Very old line-of-business HTA launchers; inventory and exclude by full command line.
name: Mshta Executing Inline VBScript or JavaScript
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\mshta.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:MSHTA.EXE) AND (process.command_line:(*vbscript\:* OR *javascript\:* OR *about\:*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects net.exe / net1.exe listing local users or local group membership. Individually this is low-fidelity (helpdesk does it daily); it is shipped at low severity as a building block for correlation with other activity from the same process tree, and to keep discovery visible in coverage.
false_positives: Administrators and helpdesk staff; use for correlation rather than alerting on its own.
name: Local Users or Administrators Enumerated via net.exe
query: ((process.executable.caseless:(*\\net.exe OR *\\net1.exe)) OR (process.pe.original_file_name:(net.exe OR net1.exe))) AND ((process.command_line:(*\ user OR *\ users)) OR process.command_line:*\ localgroup*) AND (NOT process.command_line:*\ \/domain*)

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects netsh adding an inbound allow rule to Windows Defender Firewall. Attackers open ports for C2 listeners, ad-hoc file servers or lateral movement; legitimate installers normally use the firewall API or MSI actions rather than spawning netsh.
false_positives: Software installers (game launchers, developer tools) that shell out to netsh; exclude by parent process.
name: Inbound Firewall Allow Rule Added via netsh
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\netsh.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:netsh.exe) AND (process.command_line:*firewall* AND process.command_line:*add*) AND (process.command_line:(*action\=allow* OR *mode\=enable*)) AND (process.command_line:*dir\=in* OR (process.command_line:*portopening* AND process.command_line:*netsh\ firewall*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects ntdsutil creating Install-From-Media (IFM) output, which writes a copy of ntds.dit and the SYSTEM hive to a folder. Together they contain every domain account's password hash.
false_positives: Planned domain controller promotion from media; correlate with a change record.
name: NTDS.dit Export via ntdsutil IFM
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\ntdsutil.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:ntdsutil.exe) AND (process.command_line:*ifm* AND process.command_line:*create*)

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects PowerShell started with a hidden window, no profile and a Base64-encoded command. Each flag on its own is common in admin tooling; together they are the default launcher of Empire, Covenant, Cobalt Strike and most commodity loaders. Abbreviated flags (-w 1, -nop, -e, -ec, -enc) are covered because PowerShell accepts any unambiguous prefix.
false_positives: Some RMM and patching agents run hidden encoded PowerShell; baseline by parent process and exclude.
name: Hidden PowerShell With Encoded Command (C2 Stager Pattern)
query: ((process.executable.caseless:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe)) OR (process.pe.original_file_name:(PowerShell.EXE OR pwsh.dll))) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-w\ hidden* OR *\ \/w\ hidden* OR *\ –w\ hidden* OR *\ —w\ hidden* OR *\ ―w\ hidden*) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-w\ h\ * OR *\ \/w\ h\ * OR *\ –w\ h\ * OR *\ —w\ h\ * OR *\ ―w\ h\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-w\ 1\ * OR *\ \/w\ 1\ * OR *\ –w\ 1\ * OR *\ —w\ 1\ * OR *\ ―w\ 1\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-wi\ hidden* OR *\ \/wi\ hidden* OR *\ –wi\ hidden* OR *\ —wi\ hidden* OR *\ ―wi\ hidden*) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-win\ hidden* OR *\ \/win\ hidden* OR *\ –win\ hidden* OR *\ —win\ hidden* OR *\ ―win\ hidden*) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-window\ hidden* OR *\ \/window\ hidden* OR *\ –window\ hidden* OR *\ —window\ hidden* OR *\ ―window\ hidden*) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-windowstyle\ hidden* OR *\ \/windowstyle\ hidden* OR *\ –windowstyle\ hidden* OR *\ —windowstyle\ hidden* OR *\ ―windowstyle\ hidden*) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-windowstyle\ 1\ * OR *\ \/windowstyle\ 1\ * OR *\ –windowstyle\ 1\ * OR *\ —windowstyle\ 1\ * OR *\ ―windowstyle\ 1\ *)) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-e\ * OR *\ \/e\ * OR *\ –e\ * OR *\ —e\ * OR *\ ―e\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-ec\ * OR *\ \/ec\ * OR *\ –ec\ * OR *\ —ec\ * OR *\ ―ec\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-en\ * OR *\ \/en\ * OR *\ –en\ * OR *\ —en\ * OR *\ ―en\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-enc\ * OR *\ \/enc\ * OR *\ –enc\ * OR *\ —enc\ * OR *\ ―enc\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-enco* OR *\ \/enco* OR *\ –enco* OR *\ —enco* OR *\ ―enco*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects reg.exe saving or exporting the SAM, SECURITY or SYSTEM hive. SAM plus SYSTEM is enough to recover local account NTLM hashes offline; SECURITY adds LSA secrets and cached domain credentials.
false_positives: Rare backup scripts that export entire hives.
name: Credential Registry Hive Saved via reg.exe
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\reg.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:reg.exe) AND (process.command_line:(*\ save\ * OR *\ export\ *)) AND (process.command_line:(*hklm\\sam\ * OR *hklm\\sam\"* OR *hkey_local_machine\\sam\ * OR *hkey_local_machine\\sam\"* OR *hklm\\security\ * OR *hklm\\security\"* OR *hkey_local_machine\\security\ * OR *hkey_local_machine\\security\"* OR *hklm\\system\ * OR *hklm\\system\"* OR *hkey_local_machine\\system\ * OR *hkey_local_machine\\system\"*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects regsvr32 invoking scrobj.dll with /i: pointing at a URL. This is the "Squiblydoo" technique: the signed binary downloads and executes a .sct scriptlet, bypassing application allow-listing.
false_positives: None expected.
name: Regsvr32 Loading a Remote COM Scriptlet (Squiblydoo)
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\regsvr32.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:REGSVR32.EXE) AND process.command_line:*scrobj* AND (process.command_line:(*\-i\:http* OR *\/i\:http* OR *–i\:http* OR *—i\:http* OR *―i\:http*) OR process.command_line:(*\-i\:ftp* OR *\/i\:ftp* OR *–i\:ftp* OR *—i\:ftp* OR *―i\:ftp*) OR process.command_line:(*\-i\:\\\\* OR *\/i\:\\\\* OR *–i\:\\\\* OR *—i\:\\\\* OR *―i\:\\\\*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects schtasks.exe /create where the task action (/tr) runs PowerShell, cmd, a script host or mshta. Pairs with the Security 4698 rule: this one sees who ran schtasks and from where, 4698 sees the task regardless of the API used to register it.
false_positives: Admin and software-deployment scripts that schedule PowerShell maintenance jobs; exclude by task name.
name: Scheduled Task Created to Run a Script Interpreter
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\schtasks.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:schtasks.exe) AND process.command_line:(*\ \-create\ * OR *\ \/create\ * OR *\ –create\ * OR *\ —create\ * OR *\ ―create\ *) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-tr\ * OR *\ \/tr\ * OR *\ –tr\ * OR *\ —tr\ * OR *\ ―tr\ *) AND (process.command_line:(*powershell* OR *pwsh* OR *cmd.exe\ \/c* OR *cmd\ \/c* OR *wscript* OR *cscript* OR *mshta* OR *rundll32*)))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects services.exe starting cmd.exe or PowerShell as a service binary. Real services are compiled executables; a shell as the service image is how PsExec-style tools (Impacket psexec/smbexec, Empire, Metasploit) turn "create a remote service" into "run my command as SYSTEM".
false_positives: Badly packaged third-party services that wrap a batch file; inventory and exclude by command line.
name: Service Control Manager Spawning a Shell Directly
query: process.parent.executable.caseless:*\\services.exe AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects vssadmin or wmic creating a volume shadow copy. Attackers create a snapshot to read locked files such as ntds.dit, SAM and SYSTEM. Backups normally go through the VSS API, not these command-line tools.
false_positives: Administrators scripting snapshots before maintenance.
name: Volume Shadow Copy Created From the Command Line
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\vssadmin.exe AND (process.command_line:*create* AND process.command_line:*shadow*)) OR (process.executable.caseless:*\\wmic.exe AND (process.command_line:*shadowcopy* AND process.command_line:*create*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects wevtutil clearing an event log, disabling it, or pointing the Security log at a different file. Redirecting the log file is quieter than clearing it: no 1102 event is written, and new events land somewhere nobody collects.
false_positives: Golden-image build pipelines that clear logs before capture.
name: Event Log Cleared or Redirected via wevtutil
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\wevtutil.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:wevtutil.exe) AND ((process.command_line:(*\ cl\ * OR *\ clear\-log\ *)) OR ((process.command_line:(*\ sl\ * OR *\ set\-log\ *)) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-lfn\:* OR *\ \/lfn\:* OR *\ –lfn\:* OR *\ —lfn\:* OR *\ ―lfn\:*) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-logfilename\:* OR *\ \/logfilename\:* OR *\ –logfilename\:* OR *\ —logfilename\:* OR *\ ―logfilename\:*) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-e\:false* OR *\ \/e\:false* OR *\ –e\:false* OR *\ —e\:false* OR *\ ―e\:false*) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-enabled\:false* OR *\ \/enabled\:false* OR *\ –enabled\:false* OR *\ —enabled\:false* OR *\ ―enabled\:false*))))

subtechnique.name: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects WmiPrvSE.exe starting a command interpreter. Win32_Process.Create, whether called locally or remotely over DCOM (wmic /node, Invoke-WmiMethod, Impacket wmiexec, Empire invoke_wmi), executes the new process as a child of WmiPrvSE, so this catches WMI-based execution regardless of the client tool.
false_positives: SCCM/MECM and some monitoring agents run scripts via WMI; exclude their specific command lines.
name: WMI Provider Host Spawning a Shell or Script Host
query: (process.parent.executable.caseless:*\\WmiPrvSE.exe AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe))) AND (NOT process.command_line:*WerFault*)

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects creation of HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\MiniNt. The key tells Windows it is running in WinPE; after the next reboot the Event Log service stops writing, so every downstream detection goes blind while the machine otherwise looks healthy.
false_positives: None on a running OS; MiniNt only exists legitimately inside WinPE images.
name: MiniNt Registry Key Created to Silence Event Logging
query: registry.path:*\\Control\\MiniNt

subtechnique.name: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects ProcessCreationIncludeCmdLine_Enabled being set to 0, which strips the command line from Security event 4688. Many command-line detections (including several in this repository) stop working on hosts that rely on 4688 rather than Sysmon.
false_positives: A GPO change that intentionally disables command-line auditing; confirm against change records.
name: Process Command-Line Auditing Disabled
query: registry.path:*\\Policies\\System\\Audit\\ProcessCreationIncludeCmdLine_Enabled AND winlog.event_data.Details:"DWORD \(0x00000000\)"

subtechnique.name: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects the Windows Event Log service being set to Disabled (Start = 4) through the registry. Done directly in the registry, it avoids the sc.exe / Set-Service command lines most detections watch for.
false_positives: None.
name: Event Log Service Start Type Set to Disabled
query: registry.path:*\\Services\\EventLog\\Start AND winlog.event_data.Details:"DWORD \(0x00000004\)"

subtechnique.name: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects a per-user ms-settings shell\open\command handler being written. Auto-elevating binaries such as fodhelper.exe and computerdefaults.exe read this key from HKCU before HKLM, so a standard user can make them launch any command at high integrity without a UAC prompt.
false_positives: None known.
name: UAC Bypass via ms-settings Protocol Handler Hijack
query: registry.path:(*\\ms\-settings\\shell\\open\\command\\\(Default\) OR *\\ms\-settings\\shell\\open\\command\\DelegateExecute)

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects a Run or RunOnce value whose data starts PowerShell, a script host, mshta, rundll32 or regsvr32. Installers register executables under Run; registering an interpreter with inline arguments is how fileless persistence (Empire, Kovter-style loaders) survives a reboot.
false_positives: OneDrive and Teams updaters occasionally register rundll32 entries; exclude the exact Details value.
name: Run Key Persistence Launching a Script Interpreter
query: (registry.path:(*\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\* OR *\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\* OR *\\Software\\WOW6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\* OR *\\Software\\WOW6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\*)) AND (winlog.event_data.Details:(*powershell* OR *pwsh* OR *wscript* OR *cscript* OR *mshta* OR *rundll32* OR *regsvr32* OR *cmd.exe\ \/c* OR *cmd\ \/c*))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects directory replication rights (DS-Replication-Get-Changes and DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All) being exercised by an account that is not a domain controller computer account. Domain controllers replicate as MACHINE$; a user account replicating secrets is the signature of DCSync (mimikatz lsadump::dcsync, secretsdump, Empire, Covenant). Requires "Audit Directory Service Access" on domain controllers.
false_positives: Entra Connect (MSOL_*) and other identity sync services; add their service accounts to a filter.
name: DCSync - Directory Replication Requested by a User Account
query: winlog.channel:Security AND ((event.code:4662 AND winlog.event_data.AccessMask:0x100 AND (winlog.event_data.Properties:(*1131f6aa\-9c07\-11d1\-f79f\-00c04fc2dcd2* OR *1131f6ad\-9c07\-11d1\-f79f\-00c04fc2dcd2* OR *89e95b76\-444d\-4c62\-991a\-0facbeda640c*))) AND (NOT (user.name:(*$ OR MSOL_*))))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects a scheduled task created (Security 4698) inside the \Microsoft\Windows\ folder by a non-machine account. Windows' own tasks are registered by the OS or by servicing (SYSTEM, MACHINE$); attackers hide tasks among them so they blend in during triage.
false_positives: Office and Edge updaters registering tasks while running as the signed-in user; exclude by TaskName.
name: Scheduled Task Registered Under \Microsoft\Windows\ by a User
query: winlog.channel:Security AND ((event.code:4698 AND winlog.event_data.TaskName:\\Microsoft\\Windows\\*) AND (NOT (user.name:*$ OR user.id:S\-1\-5\-18)))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects a computer account being changed by ANONYMOUS LOGON with a new password-set time. Exploiting CVE-2020-1472 (Zerologon) authenticates to Netlogon with an all-zero credential and then resets the domain controller's machine account password, which Windows logs as an anonymous 4742.
false_positives: None; anonymous computer-account password changes are not a legitimate operation.
name: Zerologon - Computer Account Password Reset by ANONYMOUS LOGON
query: winlog.channel:Security AND ((event.code:4742 AND user.name:"ANONYMOUS LOGON") AND (NOT winlog.event_data.PasswordLastSet:\-))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects a new service (System 7045) whose ImagePath launches cmd, PowerShell or another interpreter, or uses an encoded command. This is the install-time half of PsExec-style execution and fires even if the service fails to start or the process creation event is missed.
false_positives: Deployment tools that install a temporary service with a script wrapper.
name: Service Installed With a Shell Command as Its Binary Path
query: winlog.channel:System AND (((winlog.provider_name:"Service Control Manager" AND event.code:7045) OR (winlog.event_data.SourceName:"Service Control Manager" AND event.code:7045)) AND (winlog.event_data.ImagePath:(*%COMSPEC%* OR *cmd.exe\ \/c* OR *cmd\ \/c* OR *powershell* OR *pwsh* OR *mshta* OR *\ \-enc\ * OR *\ \-e\ * OR *\ \-nop\ *)))

author: DaveyD347
description: Detects a permanent WMI event consumer of type CommandLine or ActiveScript being registered (Sysmon 20). Paired with a filter and binding, this gives fileless persistence that runs as SYSTEM inside WmiPrvSE and survives reboots.
false_positives: Dell, HP and Lenovo management agents; inventory known consumers and exclude by Name.
name: WMI Event Consumer Created to Run a Command or Script
query: (event.code:20 AND (winlog.event_data.Type:("Command Line" OR Script))) AND (NOT process.executable.caseless:*BVTConsumer*)
